newsitem.title: FRANCE: French state group ERAP to oust Eramet chairman.
newsitem.headline: French state group ERAP to oust Eramet chairman.

text.p: State holding group ERAP said on Wednesday that it would replace the chairman of the mining company Eramet, Yves Rambaud, on May 29 with Thierry Chambolle and would name three other members to the board of directors.

ERAP (Enterprise de Recherches et d'Activites Petrolieres) has a 55 percent stake in Eramet and the holding company's chairman, Remy Chardon, is very critical of Rambaud's handling of a politically sensitive issue involving a nickel mine in New Caledonia.
The French government, which owns ERAP, has launched a procedure to revoke a nickel mining licence held by Eramet in order to award the mine to a group of local Kanak interests.
Canada's Falconbridge is linked with the Kanak Societe Miniere de Sud Pacifique (SMSP).
ERAP said in a statement that it had sent Eramet a proposal to nominate four new candidates for membership on its board of directors.
Voting on these candidates will take place at the annual general meeting on May 29, at which ERAP has a majority of votes.

"The AGM will be asked to elect a Board of Directors whose composition will include a majority of members who are currently serving on the board and which will reflect current capital ownership and ensure needed continuity in Eramet's business operations," the statement said.

"At the close of the AGM, the new board will be presented with the nomination of Thierry Chambolle as Chairman of Eramet to succeed current Chairman Yves Rambaud, whom ERAP congratulates for his efficient management of the company," it added.
Rambaud has been hosting talks in Paris to try to settle the issue and experts will be appointed to study the problem in detail.
Chambolle, 57, is currently deputy managing director in charge of strategy and technical development at Lyonnaise des Eaux.

"Mr Chambolle will be responsible for consolidating the industrial development strategy of Eramet in its three core businesses and for creating dialogue between the industrial partners so as to find an equitable solution to the mining conflict in New Caledonia, which will respect the interests of the company, of its personnel and of its minority shareholders," the statement said.
Rambaud had criticised the government's decision to take away the mining licence, saying it would put the future of the group at stake.

He was supported by minority shareholders, among them some big U.S. investment funds which said France's handling of the Eramet case might influence their view of the partial privatisation of France Telecom, the state-owned telecommunications company.
The French government has said it would compensate Eramet for the loss of the mining licence.
On Tuesday, the nine members of the Eramet management board publicly stated their support for Rambaud in a letter to ERAP chairman Remy Chardon, who joined the Eramet board in April.
"What is important is that top officials of Eramet's main units signed the letter. This means that if Rambaud goes, all top management will have to go," a source said on Tuesday.

No-one at ERAP was available on Wednesday to comment or say who the new board members would replace. The names of the proposed board members are Michel Beaudout, Henri Guillaume and Philippe Rouvillois.
